closureConditionNote: #425 reported that a registered worktree nested under the session root zoned as own-claim, so every lane was writable from a main-rooted session. Its narrow question: is the target inside a registered worktree other than the session root. That is what landed, and all of it is on main through 1d35b804. In bfec5d4c, zoneOf (.claude/hooks/target-ownership.mjs) zones a target inside a checkout nested strictly inside the session root as that checkout's (ZONES.SIBLING), or ZONES.UNKNOWN with that checkout as owner when git would not report its identity. project-write-assert.mjs now zones every target, and inside the root it decides the answers that name another checkout as owner: a nested lane's file is denied (TARGET_NOT_OURS) whether or not the session is verified, and an in-root checkout whose identity git would not report asks (TARGET_UNRESOLVED) instead of being called ours (tools/entry/project-write-assert.test.mjs:171-195). The issue's Boundaries named target-ownership.mjs plus its test file; the lane's claim 5650087677 also named project-write-assert.mjs and its test, and the reviewed head changes all four. The candidate evidence (5650253887) shows the required cases red against the base hooks: 9 of 64 tests failed across the two changed suites. GPT HQ's PASS confirmed denial for existing and nonexistent nested-lane files and allowance for the main checkout's own file. The PASS does not certify two adjacent gaps, and neither is a condition of #425: #428 (a recursive delete of the folder that holds registered lanes reads own-claim) and #429 (a Write through a junction inside the session root into ~/.claude is allowed). Both are open, with their own work-control fields. Closing is authorized because the merge is proven and the lease is released. The project's Item closed workflow then sets Done, and the Done is read back from the board, not assumed.
